svg.aria-label: Heule 3x3 Matrix Multiplication Challenge 2: R=23 conjectured UNSAT skewed type-3 partitions

g.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: Heule 3×3 Matrix Multiplication — Challenge 2 (Conjectured-UNSAT Skewed Partitions)
10 R = 23 Brent-equation refutation targets forcing the 27 type-3 monomials into over-packed skewed clusters (2-2-3, 2-4, 3-3, 5)
1. Pigeonhole Excess (27 Type-3 Terms in 23 Products)
Tensor T₃,₃,₃ over 𝔽₂: 27 nonzero triples aᵢⱼbⱼₖcₖᵢ (δ = 1)
Each of 27 triples must appear an odd number of times across R = 23
rank-1 layers u⁽ℓ⁾ ⊗ v⁽ℓ⁾ ⊗ w⁽ℓ⁾ ⇒ excess of 27 − 23 = 4 shared slots.
702 remaining δ = 0 Brent sums must all cancel to 0 mod 2.
Balanced Packing (Challenge 1 SAT) vs Skewed Packing (Challenge 2):
Excess +4 spread over 4 products (low cross-term load; 17,000+ SAT schemes)
Excess +4 crammed into only 1–3 products ⇒ 20–22 rigid singletons!
Cross-Term Explosion in MM-23-5-A (Pinned Product M₁₀):
5 × 5 × 5 = 125 forced outer-product monomials in M₁₀ alone!
Induces 7 type-3 triples + 118 δ = 0 terms that remaining 22 singletons
must cancel mod 2 — believed impossible, yet hard for CDCL to refute.
All 10 Challenge-2 Instances (Sorted Induced Type-3 Multiplicity):
Identical Plain Base CNF (26,541 vars · 117,203–117,207 clauses · 8,019 XORs)
Differs from Challenge 1 ONLY in the 77–81 unit pins! α = 4.42 · ρ_crit = 1.82× · κ = 0.95
All 6 benchmarked solvers (CaDiCaL, Kissat, CMS CNF/XCNF, Frobenius, dense) >10 s
